lines.text: I staked my savings with a small validator I really believe in.
Then my rent went up, and I needed that money today.
lines.human: Then my rent went up, <sigh> and I needed that money today.

lines.text: But unstaking takes more than a day. And my validator would lose the stake.
Baton turns a NEAR stake into an NFT you can sell.
lines.human: Baton turns a near stake into an N F T you can sell.

lines.text: The NFT is a real NEAR account, staked with a real validator. Whoever holds the NFT owns the stake.
lines.human: The N F T is a real near account, staked with a real validator. Whoever holds the N F T owns the stake.

lines.text: When it changes hands, the stake keeps running. Only the holder changes.
I keep some NEAR ready to buy stakes at a small discount. My offer just sits on chain, waiting.
lines.human: I keep some near ready to buy stakes at a small discount. My offer just sits on chain, waiting.

lines.text: One transaction. Maya has the money. Sam holds the stake, and it keeps earning.
And look at the validator. Not one NEAR left.
lines.human: And look at the validator. Not one near left.

lines.text: So what stops a seller from keeping a way back in?
I tried. My private room is closed, and my old key is dead.
lines.human: <chuckle> I tried. My private room is closed, and my old key is dead.

lines.text: Nobody can sign for this account at all. It has no keys. And anyone can check.
This works with every validator on NEAR, today. No new token, no shared pool, and no change to NEAR.
lines.human: This works with every validator on near, today. No new token, no shared pool, and no change to near.

lines.text: I get paid to wait a day.
lines.human: <chuckle> I get paid to wait a day.

lines.text: And I got out without hurting the validator I chose.
